title: Route _fix_code_node through _run_quality_gate (no accepted overwrite)
summary: Replace the single-shot `await self._service.stream_workflow(...)` invocation in `_fix_code_node` (`src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py`) with one `await self._run_quality_gate(...)` call, threading `acceptance_criteria=state["acceptance_criteria"]` and `base_branch=state["feature_branch"]`. Keep the existing `fix_prompt` assembly, the `merger.consolidate(...)` step, and BOTH return dicts unchanged — explicitly do NOT add `accepted` (or any other key) to the return dicts. Add ONE new test in `tests/chains/test_ralph_workflow.py` using a test-local `_SequentialQualityGate` fake (mirroring the `_SequentialReviewExecutor` precedent) that asserts (a) exactly two gate invocations across the workflow, (b) fix-path kwargs match the spec, (c) `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted` reflects the PRE-MERGE gate verdict — proving the fix gate does not overwrite the terminal `accepted` signal. No graph topology change, no helper signature change, no new `WorkflowState` field, no change to `_max_fix_rounds`. Dropping `branch_name`/`create_branch` (currently passed to `stream_workflow`) is safe because `RalphLoop._execute_node` sets these per inner iteration. Wire-level SSE output becomes richer per fix round — downstream UI/log consumers will now see per-fix-round agent activity.
context:
## Problem

`_fix_code_node` (`src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py`) runs one `await self._service.stream_workflow(...)` invocation per outer fix round, with no per-iteration evaluator pressure. The pre-merge `_run_ralph_loop_node` delegates to `_run_quality_gate`, an iterative implementer + evaluator convergence loop. The parent PR extracted `_run_quality_gate` from the pre-merge node specifically to enable this second-caller path; the helper signature already matches the kwargs in scope at the fix-node call site.

## Findings that depart from the prompt's `<change_list>` (rationale)

### Finding 1 (BLOCKING): do NOT write `state["accepted"]` from `_fix_code_node`

The prompt's `<change_list>` item 1 says to write `last_iteration_event.accepted` into the outer state because "the outer `state["accepted"]` field is the routing signal for `_route_after_fix_code`". Direct code reading disproves this premise:

- The router is named `_route_after_fix` (not `_route_after_fix_code`).
- `_route_after_fix` routes on `state["merge_error"]` and `state["pr_url"]`; it never reads `state["accepted"]`.
- The only `state["accepted"]` consumers post-fix are in `_complete_node`: it sets `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted = state["accepted"]` and gates `cleanup_backup_branches` on `if state["accepted"] and state["merged"]:`.

Concrete regression risk if we follow the original directive: a fix whose inner loop exhausts iterations (`accepted=False`) but whose consolidation succeeds and whose subsequent post-merge reviewer (which always runs after the fix) ultimately accepts would (a) emit `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted=False` despite shipping working code, and (b) silently skip backup-branch cleanup. The post-merge reviewer is already the authoritative consumer-facing verdict; widening `state["accepted"]` semantics to "most-recent quality-gate verdict" demotes it.

Therefore: `_fix_code_node` adds NO new keys to either return dict. The pre-merge value of `state["accepted"]` is preserved as the terminal signal. This is a deliberate departure from the prompt directive on factual grounds; surface in the PR description.

### Finding 2: consolidation step stays

`RalphLoop._execute_node` (`src/kodezart/chains/ralph_loop.py`) pushes commits onto `ctx.ralph_branch` via `stream_workflow` but never merges that branch into anything. The outer `merger.consolidate(...)` in `_fix_code_node` is what lands fix-branch commits onto the feature branch; removing it silently abandons fix work.

### Finding 3: `base_branch=state["feature_branch"]` required

`RalphLoop._evaluate_node` calls `git.diff_summary(base_ref=ctx.base_branch, head_ref=ctx.ralph_branch)`. If we forwarded `ctx.base_branch` (= "main"), the inner diff would include every commit the feature already shipped; the fix-round changeset must be relative to the merged feature tip.

### Finding 4: TWO `stream_workflow` kwargs are dropped — safely

The current `_fix_code_node` passes `branch_name=state["feature_branch"]` and `create_branch=True` to `stream_workflow`. `_run_quality_gate` does NOT accept these (they are `AgentRunner.stream_workflow` kwargs only). Dropping them is safe because `RalphLoop._execute_node` sets `branch_name=ctx.feature_branch` and `create_branch=is_first` itself per inner iteration, preserving first-iteration semantics (fresh fix branch created off the merged feature tip; subsequent inner iterations stack on the same fix branch).

### Finding 5: SSE stream becomes richer per fix round

The current `_fix_code_node` consumes `stream_workflow` events with `async for _event in ...: pass` — it drops every event on the floor. After the change, `_run_quality_gate` already calls `writer(event)` on every inner event (assistant text, tool use/results, one `WorkflowIterationEvent` per inner iteration). Downstream UI/log consumers will now see per-fix-round agent activity. Surface in PR description for consumer flagging.

## Documentation consulted (first-party quotes)

- **LangGraph `get_stream_writer`** — https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/config/get_stream_writer. Quoted: *"Access LangGraph StreamWriter from inside a graph node or entrypoint task at runtime."* Signature: `get_stream_writer() -> StreamWriter`. Async use requires Python ≥ 3.11; `pyproject.toml` pins ≥ 3.12 so the existing `writer = get_stream_writer()` in every node body is current.
- **LangGraph `stream_mode="custom"`** — https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming. Quoted: *"Set `stream_mode=\"custom\"` when calling `.stream()` or `.astream()` to get the custom data in the stream."* Matches `RalphWorkflowEngine.run`'s `astream(..., stream_mode="custom")` consumer.
- **pytest-asyncio auto mode** — https://pytest-asyncio.readthedocs.io/en/latest/concepts.html#test-discovery-modes. Quoted: *"In auto mode pytest-asyncio automatically adds the asyncio marker to all asynchronous test functions."* `pyproject.toml` sets `asyncio_mode = "auto"`; the new async test needs no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` decorator.
- **pytest `monkeypatch.setattr`** — https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/how-to/monkeypatch.html. Quoted signature: `monkeypatch.setattr(obj, name, value, raising=True)`; auto-reverted at test teardown. (Cited only as the patch-mechanism baseline; the new test does NOT use `monkeypatch` — see test design below.)

## Test design rationale

The previous draft prescribed `monkeypatch.setattr(engine, "_run_quality_gate", recorder)` — a private-method swap that violates the file's hexagonal idiom (every existing fix-node test exercises behavior through port-level fakes, not private attribute patching). This revision uses a test-local `_SequentialQualityGate` fake that mirrors the in-tree `_SequentialReviewExecutor` precedent. Two scripted evaluations let the test prove the non-overwrite invariant: pre-merge gate returns `accepted=True`, fix gate returns `accepted=False`, terminal `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted` remains `True` — proving `_fix_code_node` does not propagate the fix gate's verdict to the outer state.

requiredChanges.description: Inside `_fix_code_node`, keep the docstring, `ctx = ExecutionContext.from_configurable(config)`, `writer = get_stream_writer()`, `fix_branch = generate_ralph_branch_name(state['feature_branch'])`, the `ticket is None` / `feature_tip_sha is None` precondition raises, `pre_fix_head_sha = state['feature_tip_sha']`, the `fix_prompt` assembly, the entire `merger.consolidate(...)` flow, the `WorkflowConsolidationEvent` writer emit, and BOTH return dicts (the DIVERGENT/SOURCE_MISSING failure-branch dict and the FAST_FORWARDED/ALREADY_INTEGRATED success-branch dict) UNCHANGED. Replace the `async for _event in self._service.stream_workflow(...)` block with ONE statement: `await self._run_quality_gate(prompt=fix_prompt, repo_path=ctx.repo_path, repo_url=ctx.repo_url, feature_branch=state['feature_branch'], ralph_branch=fix_branch, base_branch=state['feature_branch'], permission_mode=ctx.permission_mode, allowed_tools=ctx.allowed_tools, acceptance_criteria=state['acceptance_criteria'], cache_key=ctx.cache_key)`. Do NOT bind the return value to a name (the `WorkflowIterationEvent` is intentionally discarded — no new field is written from it). Do NOT add `accepted` (or any other key) to either return dict; see finding #1 in the context for the regression risk and the actual-router evidence. Drop the `branch_name=state['feature_branch']` and `create_branch=True` kwargs that were on the `stream_workflow` call — `_run_quality_gate` does not accept them; `RalphLoop._execute_node` sets these internally per inner iteration (`create_branch=is_first`, `branch_name=ctx.feature_branch`), preserving first-iteration semantics.
requiredChanges.rationale: Routes the post-merge fix path through the same iterative implementer+evaluator helper the pre-merge path uses, giving fix rounds per-iteration evaluator pressure instead of one-shot termination. `base_branch=state['feature_branch']` is essential because the inner evaluator's diff base (`RalphLoop._evaluate_node` calls `git.diff_summary(base_ref=ctx.base_branch, ...)`) must be the merged feature tip, not `main`. Keeping the consolidation step is essential because `RalphLoop._execute_node` only pushes to `ralph_branch` and never lands those commits onto the feature branch — that is the outer engine's job. NOT writing `accepted` is essential because `_route_after_fix` does not read it (it reads `merge_error`/`pr_url`) and the only consumers (`_complete_node`'s `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted` emission and the `cleanup_backup_branches` gate) need the pre-merge verdict to remain authoritative — widening to 'most-recent quality-gate verdict' would silently regress shipped-and-reviewer-accepted runs when the fix gate exhausts iterations.

requiredChanges.description: Add a test-local class `_SequentialQualityGate` followed by one async test `test_fix_code_node_invokes_quality_gate_with_feature_base_branch` (or similar). Function-boundary placement: insert immediately after `test_fix_code_node_source_missing_routes_terminally`, before `test_review_uses_review_base_sha_and_review_head_sha_not_branch_refs`. The `_SequentialQualityGate` class mirrors the in-tree `_SequentialReviewExecutor` precedent: `__init__(self, evaluations: list[AcceptanceCriteriaOutput], last_commit_sha: str = 'a' * 40)` stores the script and a `self.calls: list[dict[str, object]] = []` recorder; `async def run(self, *, prompt, repo_path, repo_url, feature_branch, ralph_branch, base_branch, permission_mode, allowed_tools, acceptance_criteria, cache_key) -> AsyncGenerator[AgentEvent, None]` appends all 10 kwargs to `self.calls` as a dict literal, pops the next evaluation, and yields one `WorkflowIterationEvent(iteration=1, branch=ralph_branch, commit_sha=self._last_commit_sha, accepted=all(r.passed for r in evaluation.criteria_results), evaluation=evaluation)`. The test body: (1) constructs `executor = _SequentialReviewExecutor(review_results=[failing_review, passing_review])` to drive review-fail-then-pass; (2) constructs `gate = _SequentialQualityGate(evaluations=[make_passing_evaluation(), make_failing_evaluation()])` so the pre-merge call returns accepted=True (lets merge proceed) and the fix-path call returns accepted=False (would-be regression case); (3) constructs `merger = FakeBranchMerger(consolidation_outcomes=[ConsolidationOutcome(status=ConsolidationStatus.FAST_FORWARDED, feature_tip_sha='a' * 40), ConsolidationOutcome(status=ConsolidationStatus.FAST_FORWARDED, feature_tip_sha='c' * 40)])` — matches the explicit `consolidation_outcomes=[...]` construction pattern used by the existing `test_fix_code_node_divergent_routes_*` family; (4) builds the engine directly (`service = AgentService(executor=executor, workspace=FakeWorkspaceProvider(), persister=FakeChangePersister())`, then `RalphWorkflowEngine(service=service, quality_gate=gate, ticket_generator=FakeTicketGenerator(), merger=merger, git_base_url='https://github.com', git_remote='origin', git=FakeGitService(remote_branch_shas={'main': 'b' * 40}), cache=FakeRepoCache(), pr_creator=FakePRCreator(), ci_monitor=FakeCIMonitor(passed=True), max_fix_rounds=2, artifact_persister=None)`) mirroring the `test_workflow_review_fails_triggers_fix` construction precedent; (5) drives `events = [e async for e in engine.run(prompt='fix it', repo_path='/tmp/fake', repo_url='https://github.com/owner/repo', base_branch='main', permission_mode='bypassPermissions', allowed_tools=['Bash'])]`. Assertions: (a) `assert len(gate.calls) == 2`; (b) `fix_call = gate.calls[1]; assert fix_call['base_branch'] == fix_call['feature_branch']; assert isinstance(fix_call['base_branch'], str); assert fix_call['base_branch'].startswith('kodezart/'); assert fix_call['acceptance_criteria'] == ['Tests pass', 'No lint errors']; assert isinstance(fix_call['ralph_branch'], str); assert fix_call['ralph_branch'].startswith(fix_call['feature_branch']); assert '-ralph-' in fix_call['ralph_branch']`; (c) `complete_events = [e for e in events if isinstance(e, WorkflowCompleteEvent)]; assert len(complete_events) == 1; assert complete_events[0].accepted is True` — proves the fix gate's `accepted=False` did NOT overwrite the pre-merge `accepted=True`. All imports already present in the file (verify: `AsyncGenerator` from `collections.abc`, `WorkflowIterationEvent`, `AcceptanceCriteriaOutput`, `AgentEvent`, `ConsolidationOutcome`, `ConsolidationStatus`, `WorkflowCompleteEvent`, `FakePRCreator`, `FakeCIMonitor`, `FakeBranchMerger`, `FakeTicketGenerator`, `FakeGitService`, `FakeRepoCache`, `FakeWorkspaceProvider`, `FakeChangePersister`, `AgentService`, `RalphWorkflowEngine`, `_SequentialReviewExecutor`, `make_passing_evaluation`, `make_failing_evaluation`).
requiredChanges.rationale: Tests through the port (hexagonal idiom), not via private-method monkeypatching — matches every other fix-node test in the file. The `_SequentialQualityGate` test-local helper mirrors the existing `_SequentialReviewExecutor` precedent for cross-call distinction (a published pattern in the same file), is single-purpose, and isolates the assertion that an exhausted-fix-gate run does NOT regress the terminal `WorkflowCompleteEvent.accepted` signal. Two scripted evaluations are the minimal shape that lets the test prove the non-overwrite invariant: with both calls returning the same value, the assertion would be unobservable. Function-boundary anchors (not line numbers) survive unrelated edits to neighboring tests. Explicit `consolidation_outcomes=[FAST_FORWARDED, FAST_FORWARDED]` makes both consolidations explicit — matches the construction pattern of `test_fix_code_node_divergent_routes_to_comment_failure_when_pr_url_set` for traceability.
